en: Cold calamansi juice causes water vapor in the warm air to condense into liquid droplets on the outside of the glass.
Saltwater in coastal Philippine provinces accelerates the chemical change of iron roofing sheets into flaky red rust.
Hot water dissolves solid muscovado sugar faster than cold water because heat increases the movement of water molecules.
Direct tropical sunlight provides enough thermal energy to melt solid butter into a liquid puddle on a hot pan.
Bamboo stems possess high tensile strength and flexibility, making them ideal physical materials for building local houses.
Anaerobic bacteria break down carabao manure in sealed biodigesters to produce methane gas used for cooking.
Floodwaters from typhoons form heterogeneous suspensions where solid soil particles temporarily float in liquid water before settling.
Ripening lakatan bananas release ethylene gas, which triggers a chemical change that converts their starches into sweet sugars.
Intense heat in Zambales salt farms causes seawater to evaporate, leaving behind solid salt crystals through a physical change.
Fresh coconut sap is a highly viscous liquid that flows much slower than water due to its dissolved sugars.
Squeezed coconut milk is a colloid where tiny liquid fat droplets are evenly dispersed throughout liquid water.
Solid naphthalene mothballs slowly undergo sublimation in warm cabinets, turning directly into a gas that repels clothes moths.
